How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Finding the courses was easy but they were made public rather late, which was a bit annoying since I had to get them pre-approved at my home-uni, this delayed my OLA a lot.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The international coordinator at the faculty was available by email and phone and replied quickly.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very, I would have liked to take different courses but it was very difficult since I had to take 30 ECTS and the courses varied a lot in ECTS points, also some of the courses I would have liked had overlapping lectures.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Exploit the fact that you can shop a bit around. The registrations can be changed a week within the semester, try out some different courses in the beginning and make your final choice when you have had the first 1-2 lectures of each course. Also try out some of the courses at the Business school!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of student discounts in Mannheim: Sports are provided for free by the university institute for sports IFS, the IFS also has a gym with cheap subscription, lunch can be bought at the cafeteria (Mensa) for 3 EUR, city bikes are free the first 30min. with a max of 5 EUR per day, public transport is free for students in weekends and between 19.00-05.00

Additional comments:
questions.answer:
There is a lot of students in Mannheim creating a vibrant student life with a lot of bars and clubs.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sports e.g. soccer, volleyball, baskets etc. are provided for free by the university. The local ESN organization provides a lot of social activities in the beginning of the semester.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Depending on your field of study the university has good contacts with the local businesses and provides a lot of, guest lectures, forums and conferences for different subjects e.g. competition policy

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Mannheim is very well located for travel esp. by train. I highly recommend going to Heidelberg, Frankfurt, Munich, Paris, Stuttgart, Freiburg, Schwartzwald, Nürnberg and Berlin.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be very outgoing and engaged in the first weeks of the semester, participate in as many events as you can! Also take part in the buddy programme.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The polite way of addressing strangers e.g. addressing professors by title and last name

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Germans are very outgoing and festive. I loved the events taking place not only in and around the university but also the city of Mannheim and the surrounding cities. Don't miss out on going to Oktoberfest/Frühlingsfest it is probably the most german thing you'll ever experience

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Most important tips:
1. Housing: The studierendenwerke dorms are nice, the dorms B7, B6, G7 and Hafenstrasse are the most central. If you have money for luxury Campus 68 is a private dorm with very nice facilities.
2. If you need stuff like kitchen utensils you can rent them for free (only have to make deposit) at Infinity Mannheim
https://infinity-mannheim.de/maexchange/
3. It gets really hot in Mannheim during summer (30+ celsius)
4. Bring cash (EUR) a lot of places don't take cards.
5. If you have fees on your danish card it may be cheaper to open a german bank-account. I used the online N26 bank to avoid the 1% exchange fee of my danish bank as bank transfers in EUR are free of charge. Also many payments are done via SEPA most danish banks don't support this but the german ones do.
6. If you live within the quadrate everything is in walking distance!
7. Go to a Sneckenhof party
8. If you need practice rooms for playing music I can recommend Die Stimmgabel at Schwetzinger Str. 42, every room has a piano.
9. Mannheim may not be the most beautiful or amazing city, but it is very well located make us of this and travel around. It only takes 3 hours to get to Paris by train.
10. The university provides sports for free, use this! It is a great way to meet people in the beginning of the semester

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't  be scared of going to Mannheim because of it's reputation. The city may not be the most amazing one, but that has its advantages. Acommodation is cheap and not difficult to find. Everything is close by. Travelling by train or bus is very convenient. The city is not crowded by turists and eating out is easy and cheap.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Experiencing the south-german culture, meeting new people from all over the world and proably most importantly of all realising that living and working outside of Denmark is not difficult or hard.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Settling in at the beginning of the semester. It was harder than expected having to learn everything from scratch e.g.: Getting around the city and campus, finding friends, adapting to local rules and regulation (municipality and university) etc. But even though it was a big challenge it was also fun and exciting.
